---
title: Components
description: Bind a React component to an element of an HTML page, keep the markdown as the no-script version, and hand the component its content and props.
---

A component is a React component that takes over one element of the
rendered page. The element is written as ordinary markdown, so a reader
without JavaScript, a feed, or a search engine sees the markdown; in a
browser, a small runtime mounts the component over it. Nothing about
purely static documents changes: a page with no `components:` key ships no
runtime and no React.

```yaml
---
title: A page
components:
  - name: carousel
    src: carousel.tsx
---
```

```markdown
::: {#carousel}
- ![First](one.png)
- ![Second](two.png)
:::
```

The component is an ES module whose default export is a React component.
`src` is a file in the project: `.js` or `.mjs` ships as written; `.tsx`,
`.ts` and `.jsx` are transpiled when the page renders (types stripped, JSX
compiled), with no build step on your side. Relative imports between your
files are followed and shipped too.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import type { QuartoComponentProps } from "@quarto/components";

export default function Carousel({ children }: QuartoComponentProps) {
  const [i, setI] = useState(0);
  return <div className="carousel" onClick={() => setI(i + 1)}>{children}</div>;
}
```

`react`, `react-dom/client` and `react/jsx-runtime` resolve through an
import map to a copy of React shipped with the site under
`site_libs/quarto-react/`, so every component on the page shares one
React. Other packages are not resolved yet (`npm:` sources are planned;
see [`Q-25-3`](/errors/components/Q-25-3.qmd)).

## Declaring components

Each entry under `components:` (in the document, or in `_quarto.yml` for
every page) takes:

| Key | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | The name an element binds by. | required |
| `src` | The module, relative to the file that declares it; a leading `/` is the project root. | required |
| `export` | The module export to mount. | `default` |
| `bind` | Which elements: `"#id"` (one element) or `.class` (every element with the class). | `#<name>` |
| `content` | How the element's content reaches the component: `dom`, `ast` or `none`. | `dom` |
| `props` | A map of static props, passed as a JSON object. | none |

Quote `bind: "#id"`: an unquoted `#` starts a YAML comment.

Only Divs and Spans host components, so a block component is written as a
fenced div and an inline one as a bracketed span.

## Binding on the element

Instead of a selector in metadata, an element can name its component:

```markdown
::: {component=carousel}
...
:::

A [12 15 9 22]{component=sparkline component-props='{"width": 80}'} inline.
```

`component=<name>` refers to a declared component. A path works too and
declares the component on the spot: `component=./carousel.tsx`.
`component-props` carries per-element props as a JSON object, in single
quotes so the double quotes inside survive; it is merged over the
declaration's `props`.

## What the component receives

The props are the same in every page that mounts the component, and the
same shape the q2 preview will use when it dispatches on the element:

```ts
interface QuartoComponentProps<P = Record<string, unknown>> {
  attrs: { id: string; classes: string[]; attributes: Record<string, string> };
  props: P;              // declared props, overlaid by the element's
  children: React.ReactNode;  // the no-script content (content: dom)
  node?: Block | Inline; // the element's Pandoc AST (content: ast)
  host: HTMLElement | null;   // the element itself; null in the preview
}
```

`children` is the element's rendered content, handed back as a React
element. Render it where you want it and treat it as opaque; a component
that needs structure asks for `content: ast` and reads `node`, the
element's Pandoc JSON (`{ t: "Div", c: [attr, blocks] }`), the same
representation the preview renders from. `content: none` drops the content.

The types live in the `@quarto/components` package (`QuartoComponentProps`,
`QuartoComponent`, `defineComponent`); the page runtime does not need them,
they are for your editor.

## Building the element from Lua

A Lua filter or an [lmd cell](lmd.qmd) builds a bound element with
`quarto.component(name, props, content)`: a Div with the content and the
props attached, or a Span when the content is inline. Props are encoded by
`pandoc.json.encode`, which turns inlines and blocks into their text and a
`meta` value into plain JSON, so listing items can be passed straight
through. This is how a listing becomes interactive: declare it as
[`type: metadata`](../projects/listings.qmd#listings-as-data), build the
no-script markup, and hand the items to a component.

````markdown
---
listing:
  id: posts
  type: metadata
  contents: posts/*.qmd
components:
  - name: filter-table
    src: filter-table.tsx
---

```{lmd}
local items = meta.listings.posts.items
local rows = items:map(function(it)
  return { title = pandoc.utils.stringify(it.title), href = it["output-href"], date = it.date }
end)
local list = pandoc.BulletList(items:map(function(it)
  return {=: `{lmd} pandoc.Link(it.title, it.path)` (`{lmd} it.date`) :=}
end))
return quarto.component("filter-table", { rows = rows }, { list })
```
````

The component receives `props.rows` and `children` (the bullet list); the
page without JavaScript shows the list.

## When something goes wrong

The runtime never breaks the page: a module that fails to load or a
component that throws is logged to the browser console and the element
keeps its static content. At render time, a declaration or binding problem
is a warning with a `Q-25-*` code: no element for a binding
([`Q-25-4`](/errors/components/Q-25-4.qmd)), two components on one element
([`Q-25-5`](/errors/components/Q-25-5.qmd)), an undeclared name on an
element ([`Q-25-7`](/errors/components/Q-25-7.qmd)), or a TypeScript module
that does not compile ([`Q-25-9`](/errors/components/Q-25-9.qmd), with the
position inside the module).

Quarto's own page chrome can be taken over the same way where an option
exists for it: [`toc-component`](navigation.qmd#replacing-the-table-of-contents-with-a-component)
mounts a component over the table of contents, with the entries as
`props`.

Components are an HTML feature: other formats render the markdown and
ignore the binding. The q2 preview currently shows the static content for
bound elements; mounting the same components in the preview is planned.
